editorial.marketOverview: Friday cash trading confirms a relief rally, but Yahoo's 10:37 ET update shows Nasdaq up only 0.8% and S&P 500 up 0.7%. The earlier futures surge has not translated into equally strong cash gains. Nvidia reversed while Micron, Sandisk and Marvell showed strength.
editorial.whatChanged: Compared with 05:53 ET, the rally is now observed in cash rather than just futures, but leadership is uneven and gains narrowed. Repository score improved from -48 to -46. Open Watch update timestamp is unchanged; no new curated catalyst identified.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The WSJ yield pair of 4.921% and 4.693% implies a 22.8 bp curve, with both yields rising. Higher discount rates remain a constraint despite improving risk appetite. Oil reports disagree materially, so a confirmed oil reversal cannot be inferred. Current SOX, breadth and volatility are missing.
editorial.threeDayPath: Friday: watch whether the remaining rally survives the 13:00 ET close. Monday: restored liquidity and weekend OPEC+ developments test sustainability. Tuesday: JOLTS at 10:00 ET may reprice rates; chip earnings dates remain tentative and need issuer confirmation.
editorial.bullCase: Memory and networking leadership could broaden into a durable rebound if Nvidia stabilizes, SOX outperforms, breadth improves and volatility and yields ease. Chinese market support adds a positive global sentiment impulse.
editorial.bearCase: The opening fade and Nvidia reversal suggest fragile leadership. Rising yields and restrictive Fed expectations leave valuation risk intact; tariff and AI financing uncertainties remain unresolved. Oil supply risk is prospective, not a verified cause of today's equity moves.
editorial.watchNext: Check cash SOX versus QQQ, advance-decline breadth, VXN/VIX and synchronized oil and Treasury quotes before the early close. Reassess after weekend oil developments and verify earnings dates; monitor Tuesday JOLTS.
